output.title: Expedited Prior Authorization Decision Timeframe
output.draft_text:
Q: How long does an expedited prior authorization decision take?

A: When a prior authorization request qualifies for expedited (urgent) review, a decision is made within [expedited decision timeframe, e.g., number of hours] of receiving [the request / all required information, as the plan defines it]. For comparison, a standard (non-expedited) prior authorization decision is made within [standard decision timeframe].

Who qualifies for expedited review: A request is reviewed on an expedited basis when [criteria for expedited review, e.g., prescriber attestation that waiting for a standard decision could seriously jeopardize the member's life, health, or ability to regain maximum function].

Who can request expedited review: [who may request it, e.g., prescriber, member, authorized representative], by [submission channel(s), e.g., phone number, fax number, ePA portal].

If the request does not meet expedited criteria: [what happens, e.g., the request is processed under the standard timeframe and the member/prescriber is notified within [notification timeframe]].

If more information is needed: [whether and how the clock is paused or extended, and any extension limit].

How the decision is communicated: The decision is communicated to [the prescriber and/or member] by [notification method] within [notification timeframe].

If no decision is made within the timeframe: [what the advocate should do or tell the member, e.g., escalation path or contact].

If the expedited request is denied: The member may [appeal options and expedited appeal timeframe].
placeholders: [expedited decision timeframe, e.g., number of hours]
[the request / all required information, as the plan defines it]
[what happens if the request does not meet expedited criteria]
[whether and how the clock is paused or extended, and any extension limit]
[escalation path or contact if no decision is made within the timeframe]
author_checklist: Confirm the expedited prior authorization decision timeframe and whether it is measured in hours or business/calendar days.
Confirm when the clock starts (receipt of request vs. receipt of all required clinical information).
Confirm the standard prior authorization timeframe for comparison.
Confirm the criteria that qualify a request for expedited review and who makes that determination.
Confirm who may request expedited review and the accepted submission channels (phone, fax, ePA).
Confirm the process when a request is downgraded from expedited to standard, including notification requirements.
Confirm whether timeframes can be extended or paused for missing information, and any limits.
Confirm how and to whom decisions are communicated, and the notification timeframe.
Confirm whether timeframes differ by line of business (e.g., Commercial, Medicare Part D, Medicaid) or by state regulation, and split the unit if needed.
Confirm the escalation path if a decision is not made within the required timeframe.
Confirm appeal options and expedited appeal timeframes after a denial.
Confirm the regulatory or contractual source for each timeframe and cite it.
Remove any section that does not apply and verify no placeholder remains before approval.
